identity.title: Food Safety Plan — Ready-to-Eat Hummus and Bean Dips (Salem Plant)
identity.issuer: Willamette Valley Foods, Inc. (prepared by Dana Whitfield, PCQI; approved by Plant Manager)

scan.summary: This is the company's own written Food Safety Plan under FDA's Preventive Controls for Human Food rule (21 CFR Part 117), covering hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, supply-chain controls, records and training for the Salem hummus/bean dip line. It is a self-authored compliance program, not an agency-issued document, so it is judged against the rule it implements rather than treated as a permit with conditions.
scan.freshness_note: Document is effective May 12, 2025, so as of today (2026-09-27) it is about 16 months old. 21 CFR 117.170 requires reanalysis at least every 3 years, which would put a reanalysis due around 2028-05-12, but the plan itself states no reanalysis interval (see gap below), so this date is inferred, not documented.

gaps.title: Hazard analysis omits non-allergen chemical hazards
gaps.description: The hazard analysis table (Section 3) classifies hazards only as Allergen, Physical, or Biological. No chemical hazard category appears anywhere in the table (e.g., cleaning/sanitizer chemical residues, mycotoxins in tahini or beans, pesticide residues), even though 21 CFR 117.130(b)(1)(ii) requires known or reasonably foreseeable chemical hazards, including radiological hazards, to be evaluated.
gaps.fix: Add a chemical hazard row/analysis for each process step evaluating chemical contamination sources (e.g., sanitizer residue at blending/filling, mycotoxin risk in dry bean/tahini receiving) and document whether a preventive control is needed.

gaps.title: Approval line lacks a name and dated signature
gaps.description: The cover page states only "Approved by: Plant Manager" with no printed name and no signature date. 21 CFR 117.126(a) requires the food safety plan to be signed and dated by the owner, operator, or agent in charge, both upon initial completion and upon any reanalysis.
gaps.fix: Add the approving individual's printed name and a dated, ink or e-signature on the approval line, and repeat this each time the plan is reanalyzed or revised.

gaps.title: No documented validation of critical limits
gaps.description: Section 4 lists specific critical limits (212°F/60 minutes cook, 135°F-70°F-41°F cooling times, ATP swab pass, metal detector test-piece sizes) but nowhere does the plan cite a validation basis (scientific study, regulatory authority, or process authority letter) showing these limits actually control the identified hazards, as required by 21 CFR 117.160.
gaps.fix: Attach or reference a validation study or process authority letter for the cook and cooling steps (e.g., a thermal process validation for Salmonella/Listeria lethality and Clostridium perfringens/Bacillus cereus outgrowth control) and note it in the plan.
gaps.locator: Section 4, Preventive controls table (page 4); not in the document
gaps.quote: Minimum 212°F for 60 minutes, measured with a calibrated probe thermometer

gaps.title: Supply-chain program underspecified
gaps.description: Section 8 states only that tahini and dry beans come from approved suppliers with a third-party audit certificate and certificate of analysis, and that the quality manager maintains the approved supplier list. It does not identify which hazards are being controlled by the supplier, does not name the supply-chain-applied control(s), does not specify verification activity type/frequency (onsite audit, sampling/testing, review of records) or who conducts them, as required by 21 CFR 117.410–117.475.
gaps.fix: Expand Section 8 to state, for each raw material, which hazard is controlled by the supplier, what verification activity is used and how often, and who (a qualified individual) performs and approves it.
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

gaps.title: No stated reanalysis interval
gaps.description: The plan has no section addressing reanalysis of the food safety plan. 21 CFR 117.170 requires reanalysis at least every 3 years, whenever a significant change is made, whenever new hazard information emerges, or when a preventive control, combination of controls, or the plan as a whole is found to be ineffective.
gaps.fix: Add a section stating the reanalysis trigger events and a fixed maximum interval (at least every 3 years), with responsibility assigned to the PCQI.

gaps.title: No written recall plan
gaps.description: The plan identifies multiple hazards requiring a preventive control (Listeria monocytogenes, sesame allergen, metal fragments), which under 21 CFR 117.139(a) triggers a requirement for a written recall plan as part of the food safety plan. No recall plan section, product identification/traceback procedure, or notification procedure appears anywhere in the document.
gaps.fix: Add a written recall plan covering notification procedures (customers, distributors, FDA, Oregon Department of Agriculture), procedures for effectiveness checks, and disposition of recalled product.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.139(a), required as part of the plan under 21 CFR 117.126(b)(4)

deadlines.title: PCQI review of corrective action log
deadlines.source_line: All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed by the PCQI within seven days.

deadlines.title: PCQI review of monitoring records
deadlines.source_line: The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven working days of their creation.

deadlines.title: Metal detector manufacturer service
deadlines.source_line: the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually.

deadlines.title: Finished product Listeria testing
deadlines.source_line: Finished product is tested for Listeria monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory.

deadlines.title: Environmental monitoring trend review
deadlines.source_line: Environmental monitoring results are trended quarterly.

deadlines.title: Employee food hygiene training
deadlines.source_line: All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually.

deadlines.title: Record retention period
deadlines.source_line: All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record

facts.quote: The Salem plant operates one shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees.
facts.affects: Determines applicable FDA facility size category and training scope required under 117.4/117.180.
Sets the refrigerated shelf life driving Listeria monocytogenes growth hazard analysis and record retention expectations.

facts.quote: for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho
facts.affects: Determines which state agencies beyond Oregon (e.g., Washington, Idaho food safety authorities) may also have jurisdiction over distributed product.
Establishes the PCQI's training basis under 21 CFR 117.155(c)/117.180 and helps determine if refresher training is due.

expected_missing.title: The actual approved supplier list
expected_missing.why: Section 8 references a supplier list maintained by the quality manager, but the list itself is not attached or described further, which similar plants typically hold as a companion document.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Master Sanitation Schedule
expected_missing.why: Companies with an environmental monitoring/Listeria control program like this one usually hold a detailed master sanitation schedule beyond the brief ATP/Listeria swab description in Section 4-5.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Environmental monitoring site map
expected_missing.why: The plan names "10 sites weekly, zone 1 and 2" but no site map or zone diagram is attached, which similar RTE facilities typically maintain to support the swabbing program.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

expected_missing.title: Training records/log
expected_missing.why: The plan describes training requirements (Section 10) but the underlying training log or certificates for individual employees are not included, which similar facilities keep as supporting records.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

WILLAMETTE VALLEY FOODS, INC.
FOOD SAFETY PLAN
Ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips
Salem Plant, 1850 Fairgrounds Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97301
Effective date: May 12, 2025
Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual
(PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)
Approved by: Plant Manager
1. Facility and product description
Willamette Valley Foods produces refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips in 8-ounce and 16-
ounce sealed plastic tubs for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho. The Salem plant operates one
shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees. Products are made from cooked chickpeas or black
beans, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt and spices, blended, filled, sealed, coded and held
refrigerated at or below 41°F. Shelf life is 45 days refrigerated. Products are labeled with the allergen
statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
2. Process flow
Receiving of dry beans, tahini and other ingredients → dry storage or refrigerated storage → soaking and
cooking of beans (kettle, 212°F, 60 minutes minimum) → cooling in the blast chiller → blending with
other ingredients → filling and sealing → date coding → metal detection → refrigerated storage →
shipping.
3. Hazard analysis

4. Preventive controls

growth at cooling and to 41°F within a further 4 hours in the blast chiller 4 hours
Listeria in the Sanitation of food-contact surfaces before each Sanitation ATP swab pass before start-up; Listeria
RTE environment production run and between products; environmental spp. swabs, 10 sites weekly, zone 1 and 2
monitoring swabs weekly
Sesame allergen Allergen labeling review for every label at receipt and at Allergen Label matches the formulation sheet;
printing; product scheduling with hummus items last in washdown verified by ATP swab before
the day, followed by full washdown the next non-sesame product
Metal Metal detection of every sealed tub Process Reject at 2.0 mm ferrous, 2.5 mm non-
ferrous, 3.0 mm stainless test pieces
5. Monitoring
The kettle operator records the internal temperature and the time at the start and end of each cook batch
on the cook log. The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling
log. The sanitation lead records the ATP swab result before each start-up. The line lead runs the three
metal test pieces through the detector at start-up, every two hours, and at the end of the run, and records
the result. The quality technician reviews every label lot against the formulation sheet at receipt and signs
the label log.
6. Corrective actions
If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or
discarded, and the cause is recorded. If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded. If an ATP
swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts. If a Listeria spp. swab is
positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since
the last negative swab is held pending investigation. If the metal detector fails a test piece, all product
since the last passing test is re-run through the detector. If a label does not match the formulation, the lot
is quarantined and not used. All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed
by the PCQI within seven days.
7. Verification
The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven
working days of their creation. Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly,
and the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually. Finished product is tested for Listeria
monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory. Environmental monitoring results are trended
quarterly.
8. Supply-chain program
Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit
certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot. The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality
manager.
9. Records
All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
and are available to FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture on request. Records are reviewed and
signed by the PCQI as described in section 7.
10. Training
All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually. The PCQI holds a current
FSPCA certificate. Sanitation and line leads are trained on the monitoring procedures in this plan.
